title: Who's Who: Beatrice Halden
summary: Secretary of the Alderwick Society whose work remains part of the record of modern Eidetics.
author: Who's Who Desk
paragraphs: The Correspondent adds Beatrice Halden (1731–1802) to its Who's Who of Eideticians, recording a secretary of the Alderwick Society whose name still attends serious discussion of the Eidetic Stratum.

Halden edited the minutes of the 1764 meetings that adopted the words Eidetic Stratum and Eidetician. Though barred from voting by the Society’s rules, she forced rival researchers to state exactly what their terms meant.
Her indexed proceedings preserved dozens of observations that more celebrated members forgot to publish.

For Alderwick readers, Beatrice Halden is remembered not as an ornament to legend but as a figure whose work helps explain why Eideticians prize careful terms, repeatable evidence and a sober account of what remains unknown.
